label: F22#4 Riverwatch main Medium-r1 vs Low-r2
brief: A named trainer fight at a Meadows river lock: the river captain's water creature against the player's smaller creature. Frames: before the fight, twelve half-second frames, after, then three telegraphed attacks (start, mid, strike). Does the fight read on screen - both fighters, the telegraphs and the impacts clearly visible - and does it look like an event that belongs to the world?
defects: The captain's creature does not read as a boss: it is not convincingly larger than the player's creature
Telegraph rings or lanes are the flat magenta the art direction lists as a defect
A landed attack shows no visible impact (no splash, debris or flash where it hits)
The captain's creature renders washed-out, grey or semi-transparent (a ghost or hologram) instead of a solid creature

label: F17#6 noshafts diag Medium approach-nave
brief: Fixed views of the Crossing Hall in a Meadows village (outside approach, nave, side arches, shrine end) by day and night, one in rain, with the 1.80 m trainer as a ruler. Judge whether the Hall reads as a warm, lived-in great hall that belongs in the key art's world.
defects: The Hall reads as a bare courtyard under a cold blue-grey grade instead of a warm, furnished great hall
Structural posts sit in the camera's near field and frame or block the views
The shrine end has no warm focal point that draws the eye
